Chapter 1: First-Principles Problem Formulation — Spatial Arbitrage & Why It Turns "Phantom"

1.1 Starting From Zero: What Is Spatial Arbitrage?

In classical economics, the Law of One Price (LOP) says that if two wholesale markets i (local origin) and j (distant destination) are connected by truck transport cost Fij, the equilibrium price gap between them cannot exceed Fij. Whenever Pj − Pi > Fij, traders buy at i, ship to j, and collect riskless arbitrage.

When an Indian farmer checks an app like AGMARKNET or e-NAM every morning t, the screen displays the nominal screen spread:

ΔPscreeni→j, t  =  Pscreenj, t  −  Plocali, t    (₹ per quintal, 1 qtl = 100 kg)

Why do these numbers matter so urgently for a smallholder?

  • According to Government of India's MoSPI NSO NSS Report No. 587 (77th Round Situation Assessment Survey, PIB PRID 1753856), Indian Potato and Onion farmers harvest an average of 29.33–38.73 quintals per season—fixing our physical decision unit at one 30-quintal mini-truckload (₹1/qtl = ₹30/truck).
  • The same national survey shows the average agricultural household earns only ₹3,798/month in net crop income, while 50.2% of households carry an average debt of ₹74,121.
  • So a ₹1,000/qtl screen spread across a 30-qtl truck looks like +₹30,000 (~7.9 months of household net crop earnings) from a single dispatch!

1.2 First-Principles Decomposition: Four Hidden Frictions Between Screen and Auction Cash

Between seeing a quote on the morning of day t and unloading a non-refrigerated open truck at destination j on arrival day t + τ (τ ∈ {1, 2, 3} days), four physical and institutional frictions erode that paper spread:

  1. Cultivar / Grade Mismatch ("Apples vs. Oranges on One Screen"): Portals highlight a single crop modal price (e.g., "Onion" or "Apple"). In reality, wholesale auctions clear strictly by variety (Red vs. Desi Onion; Badshah vs. Kufri Jyoti Potato) and grade (HP Apple Grade A vs. Grade B vs. Grade C). Arriving with Grade B when buyers bid only on Grade A forces distress liquidation at another variety's Min_Price − 10%.
  2. Closed Gates & Forward-Filled Stale Quotes: Indian APMC yards observe rotating weekly closing holidays and local mandi disruptions. Price apps often forward-fill quotes up to 7 days old. Across 63,040 naive dispatches, 46.69% find zero exact-variety arrivals over 3 consecutive arrival mornings [t+τ, t+τ+2], and 58.94% either wait 1–2 days or miss exact-variety trading entirely.
  3. Winding Highways & Single-Lane Hill Roads (OSRM vs. Haversine): Straight-line Euclidean distance ("as the crow flies") systematically understates real rural and mountain highway distances and transit times. Per the Government of Himachal Pradesh Economic Survey 2025–26 (Table 28), 91.59% (39,465 / 43,091 km) of HP motorable roads are single-lane hill roads—forcing a 1.45× freight penalty and slower transit speeds.
  4. Biological Q10 Thermal/Rain Rot & Arrival Price Reversion: Open mini-trucks hauling tomatoes or onions across 35–42°C summer plains or ≥35 mm monsoon downpours lose salable weight and grade en route. Meanwhile, during the 1–3 day haul τ, regional inflows attracted by the same high screen price frequently pull arrival prices downward (arrival reversion).
Formal Definition: Phantom Spatial Arbitrage

An episode exhibits Phantom Spatial Arbitrage whenever nominal portal gain appears attractive (ΔPscreen > ₹100/qtl), yet realized net profit over local sale turns negative (ΔNeti→j,t < 0) once exact-variety availability, OSRM freight + GoI state fees, biological spoilage, and arrival prices settle.

Chapter 2: Deep Dive Into the Most Relevant Research (20 Core + 8 Mandi Papers)

In an M.Tech defense, your literature review is tested on precision: What exact theorem, econometric design, or algorithm did each paper invent, and where does that method break on Indian horticultural dispatch? Below is the complete paper-by-paper breakdown across our 5 foundational pillars (14 Stage-I papers + 6 Stage-II mechanistic/uncertainty/liquidity citations).

2.1 Pillar I: Spatial Arbitrage & Indian Mandi Market Economics

1. Robert Jensen (2007) — "The Digital Provide: Information (Technology), Market Performance, and Welfare in the South Indian Fisheries Sector"
The Quarterly Journal of Economics (QJE), 122(3):879–924 • DOI: 10.1162/qjec.122.3.879

Intuition & Method: Difference-in-differences natural experiment tracking Kerala sardine fishermen (1997–2001) across sequential mobile-tower rollouts. Before mobile coverage, boats landed fish at home beaches with zero knowledge of neighboring landing ports—leading to 5–8% dumped catch in saturated markets while nearby ports went empty. Once phones arrived at sea, captains called ahead and arbitrage equalized coastal prices.

Exact Gap Left Open: Sardines are homogeneous and coastal sea hops had negligible quality mismatch, closed-yard holidays, or mountainous single-lane road congestion. Inland Indian APMC mandis violate every one of Jensen's implicit frictionless assumptions.

2. C. S. C. Sekhar (2012) — "Agricultural Market Integration in India: An Analysis of Select Commodities"
Food Policy, 37(3):309–322 • DOI: 10.1016/j.foodpol.2012.03.002

Intuition & Method: Applies Johansen cointegration and error-correction econometric tests across Indian wholesale price series (gram, oilseeds, rice, wheat). Demonstrates that inter-state regulatory and physical barriers keep Indian wholesale markets segmented rather than frictionlessly integrated.

Exact Gap Left Open: Long-run monthly/weekly cointegration coefficients cannot diagnose why a 30-qtl truck dispatched tomorrow morning crashes into a stale variety quote or closed gate.

3. Shoumitro Chatterjee & Devesh Kapur (2016/2017) — "Six Puzzles in Indian Agriculture"
India Policy Forum (NCAER/SAGE), 13(1):185–229 • Price Variation & Market Dispersion

Intuition & Method: Granular mandi-level dispersion study showing immense spatial price spreads persist even across nearby Indian districts after adjusting for rough transport costs, attributing the wedge to APMC laws, intermediaries, and unobserved quality.

Exact Gap Left Open: Stops at macro documentation; does not decompose daily operational screen spreads into exact-variety mismatch, OSRM routing friction, ERA5 thermal spoilage, and arrival-day execution risk.

4. Negi, Birthal, Roy, & Khan (2018) — "Farmers' Choice of Market Channels & Producer Prices in India"
Food Policy, 81:106–121 • DOI: 10.1016/j.foodpol.2018.10.008

Intuition & Method: Nationally representative farm household regression analysis proving that poor road connectivity and weak market information jointly trap Indian smallholders in low-margin village-trader sales rather than competitive wholesale mandis.

Exact Gap Left Open: Cross-sectional household surveys cannot power real-time route selection, road-hour transit spoilage accounting, or uncertainty-calibrated local abstention.

5. Madaan, Sharma, Khandelwal, Goel, Singla, & Seth (2019) — "Price Forecasting & Anomaly Detection for Agricultural Commodities in India"
Proceedings of ACM COMPASS '19, pp. 52–64 • DOI: 10.1145/3314344.3332488

Intuition & Method: Flagship CS/ICTD study mining multi-year AGMARKNET onion and potato series to forecast point prices and flag hoarding/supply anomalies across mandis.

Exact Gap Left Open: Evaluates price forecasting MSE and anomaly alerts—NOT executable spatial dispatch under closed yards, variety mismatches, OSRM highways, Q10 heat shrinkage, or asymmetric selective refusal.

2.2 Pillar II: Indian Post-Harvest Loss Biology, Climate Reanalysis & Road Routing

6. Jha et al. (2015, ICAR-CIPHET) & 7. NABCONS / MoFPI (2022, PIB PRID 2151371) — National Post-Harvest Loss Surveys
ICAR-CIPHET Ludhiana (45+ crops, 173 pp.) • MoFPI Final Audit (54 crops across 292 districts, Dec 2022)

Intuition & Official Anchors: India's statutory empirical audits measuring physical weight/quality shrinkage via direct farm-to-retail weighments across 15 agro-climatic zones (fruits 6.02–15.05%, vegetables 4.87–11.61%). Crucially, NABCONS Annexure-II Table-2 isolates market/transport-stage losses: Tomato 3.25%, Onion 1.96%, Apple 1.64%, Potato 0.86%.

Exact Gap Left Open: Macro annual national averages cannot dynamically scale with corridor transit hours, 40°C summer spikes, or 35 mm rainstorms on a specific morning dispatch.

8. Hersbach et al. (2020, QJRMS) — ERA5 Global Reanalysis [& Sparks 2018 NASA POWER; Luxen & Vetter 2011 OSRM]
QJRMS 146(730):1999–2049 (DOI: 10.1002/qj.3803) • Sparks JOSS (NASA POWER) • Luxen & Vetter ACM SIGSPATIAL (OSRM)

Intuition & Method: ERA5 assimilates atmospheric physics onto a gap-free 0.1°/0.25° global grid (matching NASA POWER 0.5° for 2017–2023), solving missing rural weather-station coverage across India; OSRM uses Contraction Hierarchies on OpenStreetMap road graphs to query real turning highways in sub-millisecond speed.

Exact Gap Left Open: Meteorological grids and contraction-hierarchy routers existed separately—MandiGuard couples them causally (forecasted NWP at decision time vs. realized ERA5 in evaluation) to price corridor Q10 rot.

2.3 Pillar III: Selective Prediction, Asymmetric Reject Option & Conformal Uncertainty

9. C. K. Chow (1970) — "On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff"
IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, 16(1):41–46 • DOI: 10.1109/TIT.1970.1054406

First-Principles Math: Given decision loss c_error and abstention cost c_reject, Chow proved the Bayes-optimal predictor abstains whenever maximum posterior certainty falls below 1 − (c_reject / c_error). In dispatch, a false-positive truck crash costs sunk freight + rot + diversion (c_error ≫ 0), whereas refusing returns safe local price (c_reject = 0 net opportunity).

10. Franc, Průša, & Voráček (2023, JMLR) & 11. Angelopoulos & Bates (2023, FnTML) [+ Gibbs & Candès 2021 ACI]
Franc et al.: JMLR 24(11):1–49 • Angelopoulos & Bates: FnTML 16(4):494–591 (DOI: 10.1561/2200000101)

Intuition & Honest Gap: Franc et al. prove risk–coverage optimal selective rules rely on monotonic calibrated uncertainty scores. Angelopoulos & Bates formalize distribution-free split conformal prediction: subtracting the (1−α) empirical residual quantile wraps any black-box tree in guaranteed coverage under i.i.d. exchangeability. Because daily agricultural prices shift across harvest/monsoon regimes, we explicitly treat conformal bounds as empirical chronological calibration verified out-of-sample (78.85% val / 79.07% holdout) and test Gibbs & Candès (2021) Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI) in Appendix A.1.

2.4 Pillar IV: Budgeted Feature Acquisition & Uncertainty-Gated Tool Calling

12. Yao et al. (2023, ICLR — ReAct), 13. Kachuee et al. (2019, ICLR — Opportunistic Learning), 14. Han et al. (2024, ACL — UALA)
ReAct: ICLR '23 (Notable-Top-5%) • Opportunistic Learning: ICLR '19 • UALA: Findings of ACL '24, pp. 6662–6685

Intuition & Design Bridge: Yao et al. showed tool grounding eliminates hallucinations—but polling every external API upfront wastes budget. Kachuee et al. formalized acquiring costly features sequentially under test-time query budgets, while Han et al. (UALA) proved uncalibrated confidence fails unless gated by calibrated uncertainty quantiles on held-out calibration buffers. MandiGuard implements this cleanly—without LLM fragility or latency—as an ascending-cost deterministic cascade (T1 → T2 → T3 → T4).

2.4b Pillar V: Selective Labels, Heteroscedastic Conformal, CRC & Grade Liquidity (6 Stage-II Papers)

15. Lei et al. (2018, JASA) & 16. Romano, Patterson, & Candès (2019, NeurIPS — CQR)
Lei et al.: JASA 113(523):1094–1111 (10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116) • Romano et al.: NeurIPS 32:3538–3548

Intuition & Gap Addressed: Proves why constant/pooled split conformal residual quantiles only satisfy marginal coverage while failing conditional coverage when input noise variance is heteroscedastic (motivating CQR). In Stage II (Exp 16), we quantify how pooled cushions inside Stage-I mandis produce a 21.07–22.66 pp coverage swing between calm Q1 (90.46% Holdout) and volatile Q4 (67.80% Holdout) markets.

17. Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, & Schuster (2024, ICLR Spotlight — Conformal Risk Control)
ICLR 2024 (OpenReview; arXiv:2208.02814)

Intuition & Honest Method Boundary: Generalizes conformal calibration beyond 0–1 errors to monotone bounded loss functions via empirical threshold sweeping (n_loss + 1)/(n_disp + 1) ≤ β. Stage-II MandiGuard-CRC adapts this ratio to calibrate tail risk weight λ* = 0.15 strictly on Val_2025H1—explicitly noting we do not claim Theorem 1 exchangeability guarantees under non-exchangeable monsoon shifts and post-selection denominators.

18. Lakkaraju, Kleinberg, Leskovec, Ludwig, & Mullainathan (2017, ACM KDD — Selective Labels)
KDD '17, pp. 275–284 • DOI: 10.1145/3097983.3098066

Intuition & Domain Autopsy: Formalizes how fitting or auditing models only on observed ("uncensored") cases creates severe blind spots when selection correlates with missingness. Exp 16 proves Stage-I's dropna(target_ret) discarded 55.83% of raw 2024 routes and understated 3-day Q20 downside drops up to 2.54×.

19. Aparajita Goyal (2010, AEJ: Applied Economics) & 20. Levi et al. (2020, PNAS)
Goyal: AEJ: Applied 2(3):22–45 (10.1257/app.2.3.22) • Levi et al.: PNAS 117(5):2366–2371 (10.1073/pnas.1906854117)

Intuition & Domain Autopsy: Proves in rural MP soy kiosks and Karnataka unified bidding platforms (ReMS) that auction liquidity & grading fragmentation govern farmer realization. Explains why sparse Apple sub-grade reporting (Grade A/Range-1) fooled Stage-I T1 rolling counters into blocking 77.82% of holdout B2-profitable Apple opportunities.

Chapter 3: Under the Hood — Math, Physics, HGBR Trees, Conformal LCB & Worked Numerics

3.1 Chronological Split Firewall & Causal Feature Mechanics

Before evaluating any dispatch rule, 2024–2026 panel data (260,043 daily market rows across 178 core yards ranked strictly on 2024 trading days to kill survivorship bias) passes through a hard temporal firewall:

3.2 Step 0 & Tool T1: Free Shortlist and Yard Vitality Gate (verify_vitality_and_variety)

Step 0 (0 API Calls): Compare today's local exact-variety price Plocali,t against headline ≤7-day modal prices at all intra-state mandis within 15 ≤ road_km ≤ 500 km. Retain those with screen_spread = Pscreenj,t − Plocali,t > ₹100/qtl, and keep top Kmax = 5.

Tool T1 (+1 API Call per candidate): Queries exact-variety trading history at yard j up to date t (never using future dates). Must satisfy all 3 rules simultaneously (mandiguard_agent.py:137-144):

T1_OK  ⟺  (dest_age_days ≤ 3)  ∧  (dest_open_prob_14d ≥ 0.50)  ∧  (dest_dow_open_rate ≥ 0.35)

Where dest_dow_open_rate = (k + 1) / (n + 2) is the Laplace-smoothed historical probability that yard j actively trades that exact variety on target arrival weekday (dow(t) + τ) mod 7 over its last n ≤ 12 occurrences prior to day t. For example, if over the past 10 Sundays a yard opened only 1 time, (1+1)/(10+2) = 0.167 < 0.35 → pruned immediately (CLOSED_YARD_RISK).

3.3 Tool T2: OSRM Highway Freight, Transit Lag & GoI Statutory Fees (compute_freight_inr)

OSRM routing returns true highway distance dijroad and car travel hours. Multiplied by 1.35× heavy truck factor (plus 1.25× HP mountain factor) and 4.0 h loading/auction buffer gives truck_hours, mapping morning dispatch into discrete auction arrival lags: τ = 1d (≤4.5 h), τ = 2d (4.5–8.5 h), or τ = 3d (>8.5 h).

Fij  =  (35  +  0.45 · mHP · dijroad) · multfreight  +  𝕀[cross_district] · γstate, crop · Plocali,t

GoI Parameters: mHP = 1.45 in HP (91.59% single-lane roads, GoHP Survey 2025–26), 1.0 elsewhere. Statutory fee γstate,crop (GoI PIB 154554): 0.5% (KA, GJ, HP-Veg), 1.0% (MH, HP-Apple), 1.5% (MP, UP). Prunes immediately if Prefj,t − Plocali,t − Fij ≤ 0 (FREIGHT_EXCEEDS_SPREAD).

Worked Numerics: MP Tomato (200 km, ₹1,400 local): 35 + 0.45×1.0×200 + 0.015×1,400 = ₹146.00/qtl. HP Apple (180 km mountain road, ₹4,000 local): 35 + 0.45×1.45×180 + 0.010×4,000 = 35 + 117.45 + 40 = ₹192.45/qtl.

3.4 Tool T3: Q10 Biological Thermal Spoilage & Monsoon Rain Penalty (compute_spoilage_fraction)

Anchored directly to MoFPI/NABCONS (2022) 24-hour market-level loss rates at 20°C (Tomato 3.25%, Onion 1.96%, Apple 1.64%, Potato 0.86%), biological respiration scales exponentially via Q10 = 2 per +10°C rise plus excess humidity (>70% RH) and heavy rain (≥35 mm/day):

Q10 = 2(Teff − 20)/10  |  FRH = 1 + 0.25·max(0, RHeff−7030)  |  sij(w) = min(0.55, [s0,c·hij+24w24·Q10·FRH + 0.02·𝕀(Rain≥35)]·multspoil)

At Rain ≥ 35 mm/day, T3 also subtracts RainPen = 0.50 × Pref × intra_spread14d (price shift toward yard minimum). Example (40°C May MP Tomato, 6 h drive, dry 50% RH): Q10 = 2² = 4×, shat = 0.0325 × (6/24) × 4 × 1 = 3.25% (-₹65/qtl on ₹2,000). Under 42 mm storm at 30°C (8h, 85% RH): 0.0325×(8/24)×2×1.125 + 0.02 = 4.44% plus 50% grade downgrade!

3.5 Tool T4 (Part A): Under the Hood of HistGradientBoostingRegressor (17 Causal Features)

Instead of predicting raw ₹/qtl (uncomparable across ₹600 potatoes and ₹10,000 apples), we predict bounded arrival return y = clip((Parr_d0 − Pref)/Pref, -0.60, +0.80) from 17 strictly causal features (dates ≤ t):

CategoryExact Features in FEATURE_COLSPhysical / Market Signal (Strictly Computed Using ≤ t Only)
Logistics/Vitality (4)tau_days, dest_age_days, dest_open_prob_14d, dest_dow_open_rateArrival lag {1,2,3}, quote staleness, 14d open fraction, arrival-weekday activity rate.
Momentum & Risk (7)dest_ret_1d, 3d, 7d, 14d; dest_vol_14d, intra_spread_14d, level_ratio_30dPrice trend & mean-reversion spike ratio (Pt/median_30d), 14d volatility, (Modal−Min)/Modal.
Macro & Encodings (6)state_hub_ret_7d, arrival_dow, month_sin, month_cos, commodity_code, state_codeStatewide 7d momentum, cyclical seasonality, native integer categories for trees.
How Histogram GBDT Works Inside arrival_forecaster.py (255-Bin Speed + L2 Leaves)

Hyperparameters: max_iter = 180 trees, max_depth = 5, min_samples_leaf = 80, learning rate η = 0.05, L2 penalty λ = 1.0. Before tree building starts, each numeric column is quantized into ≤255 histogram bins once—reducing split search from O(N log N) to O(255) and giving 0.09 ms/query CPU speed.

Numeric Step Trace (4 Sample Trips): Suppose true arrival returns are y = [-0.10, -0.05, +0.02, +0.05].
1. F0 = mean(y) = -0.02 → residuals (negative gradients of ½(y−F)²) are g = [-0.08, -0.03, +0.04, +0.07].
2. Split bin dest_level_ratio_30d > 1.25 groups spiked markets {-0.08, -0.03} left and stable markets {+0.04, +0.07} right.
3. L2-regularized optimal leaf weight is w = (∑ gi) / (nleaf + λ): Left = (-0.11)/(2+1) = -0.0367, Right = (+0.11)/3 = +0.0367.
4. Shrinkage update: F1 = -0.02 + 0.05 × (-0.0367) = -0.0218. Repeating 180 trees smoothly captures non-linear price reversion!

3.8 Under the Hood of Stage-II MandiGuard-CRC (uncensored_crc_forecaster.py)

Why Switch From Stage-I Censored Return LCB to Stage-II Dual-Head Uncensored Scoring?

Stage-I dropped missing arrival rows (dropna(target_ret), losing 55.83% of raw 2024 routes) and subtracted one crop-pooled residual buffer (causing 90.46% calm vs 67.80% volatile coverage). Stage-II fixes both with two frozen 2024 HistGradientBoosting heads trained on every settled corridor (arrival_date + 2d ≤ 2024-12-31) using full uncensored payoff Y_full = real_delta_net_inr (so closed-yard crashes are directly visible during training):

ScoreCRC(m)  =  μ̂(m)  −  λ* · Ploc · p̂loss(m)       [Dispatch iff ScoreCRC(m*) > ₹50/qtl & μ̂(m*) > ₹50/qtl]

Validation Calibration (Val_2025H1, N = 42,794, Zero Holdout Tuning): Fitting regression μ̂ + raw HistGradientBoostingClassifier.predict_proba loss-risk estimator p̂loss on 274,296 settled 2024 routes (t1_ok & static_net > 0) with 1.20× Euclidean Step-0 sorting, we sweep λ ∈ {0.00, 0.05, ..., 1.20} on clean Val_2025H1 (arr_dt ≤ 2025-05-31) and stop at the first feasible grid point (break) satisfying (nloss(λ) + 1) / (ndisp(λ) + 1) ≤ βtarget = 0.095 → freezing λ* = 0.15 for MandiGuard-CRC (Val mean ₹365.46/qtl, 9.15% LTR; Rung 2 strict T1 freezes at λ* = 0.10, ₹358.52/qtl, 9.34% LTR). Statistical Boundary: Adapts Angelopoulos et al. (2024) as an empirical validation heuristic without claiming exchangeability Theorem 1 guarantees.

Worked Numerics (Calm vs Volatile Comparison, Ploc = ₹1,400/qtl): (a) Safe Calm Corridor: μ̂ = +₹220/qtl, p̂loss = 0.04 → Penalty = 0.15 × 1,400 × 0.04 = -₹8.40 → Score = +₹211.60/qtl > ₹50 (Stage I over-buffered calm routes, while CRC unlocks them!).
(b) Volatile 3-Day Stale Corridor: μ̂ = +₹140/qtl, p̂loss = 0.55 → Penalty = 0.15 × 1,400 × 0.55 = -₹115.50 → Score = +₹24.50/qtl < ₹50 → PRUNE cleanly even if point prediction looks profitable! Additionally, Grade-Aware T1 (fresh0 | strict) admits fresh same-day quotes (age = 0 with open_prob_14d ≥ 0.20 and dow_open_rate ≥ 0.25) alongside persistent routes so sub-grade Apple tags aren't falsely blocked.

4.2 Four Core Evaluation Metrics (Plus Conditional vs. Unconditional Clarity)

Suppose over 10 episodes, a policy stays home (₹0) twice and dispatches 8 times with outcomes [-300, -100, +50, +100, +200, +300, +400, +550]:

  1. Mean Net Gain (Unconditional): Sum across ALL 10 episodes / 10 = ₹1,200 / 10 = +₹120/qtl (+₹3,600/truck). Note: Conditional gain on dispatched trips is ₹1,200 / 8 = +₹150/qtl, and Mean = Cond_Gain × Dispatch_Rate.
  2. Loss-Trip Rate (LTR — Conditional Dispatched Loss Rate): Fraction of dispatched trucks losing money = 2 / 8 = 25.0%. (Unconditional episode loss probability across all 10 episodes is 2 / 10 = 20.0% — the exact target used in confirmatory Hypothesis H3!).
  3. Worst-10% Loss (CVaR_10%): Sort all 10 episodes worst-to-best: [-300, -100, 0, 0, +50, ...]; average the bottom 10% (worst 1 entry) = -₹300/qtl. On holdout (N = 69,526), CVaR_10% averages the worst 6,952 episodes.
  4. Live API Calls / Query: Mean online requests executed per episode before issuing DISPATCH or REFUSE_PHANTOM_SPREAD.

4.3 Under the Hood: Two-Way Cluster Bootstrap (R = 5,000) & Holm–Bonferroni

Why would a textbook paired t-test produce fake significance? Because mandi trips cluster two ways simultaneously: (a) Serial Correlation within the same origin market over consecutive days, and (b) Spatial Correlation across markets sharing state monsoon/export shocks in the same week.

Two-Way Cluster Bootstrap Matrix Algebra (bootstrap.py, 174 Origin Mandis × 23 Two-Week Blocks)
Concrete 3×3 Bootstrap Matrix Calculation (Verify on Whiteboard!)

Suppose 3 mandis × 3 two-week blocks have SUM = [[300,-100,200], [100,400,0], [500,100,300]] and uniform CNT = 10 per cell. If draw r samples mandis [M1, M1, M3] (mw = [2, 0, 1]) and blocks [B2, B3, B3] (bw = [0, 1, 2]), each cell (m,b) gets weight mw[m] × bw[b]: SUM·bw = [0(300)+1(-100)+2(200)=300, ..., 0(500)+1(100)+2(300)=700]. Multiplying by mw gives num = 2×300 + 0 + 1×700 = 1,300; denominator den = 2×(30) + 1×(30) = 90; thus replicate mean is 1,300 / 90 = +₹14.44. Across 5,000 draws, the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles form the exact Two-Way CI!

Chapter 6: Complete Synopsis & Thesis Viva Defense Playbook

6.1 Word-for-Word Spoken Scripts (1-Min Elevator, 5-Min Synopsis & 15-Min Viva)

1-Minute Elevator Pitch: "Every morning, price apps tell Indian vegetable and apple farmers that a distant mandi 200 km away pays ₹500–₹1,300/qtl more than their home yard. Across 69,526 holdout dispatch opportunities in six Indian states (Maharashtra, UP, Karnataka, MP, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh), 58.94% of naive price-chasing dispatches hit closed yards or missing variety auctions and 40.46% lose money—a gap we call Phantom Spatial Arbitrage, where unfiltered point-ML loses even more often (45.28%). My thesis follows a strict Two-Stage architecture verified across nearly 10 years of AGMARKNET records (42.72M raw rows, dual-tier verified in Exp 14 against 172 official data.gov.in XML keys and a 149-day AGMARKNET 2.0 export of 2,042 keys at 100.00% Min/Max/Modal parity): In Stage I (Pre-Registered), MandiGuard v1 (T1 → T2 → T3 → T4 + frozen 2024 HGBR + causal 80% conformal LCB) beats naive portals by +₹102.78/qtl (+₹3,083.5 per 30-qtl truck), cuts episode losses by 37.29 pp vs point-ML, and saves 44.4% external calls, while tying fresh-road greedy B2 on mean (+₹6.13/qtl, p = 0.27). In Stage II ([POST-DIAGNOSTIC / VALIDATION-CALIBRATED], Exp 16–17), our autopsy showed dropna censoring understated 3-day downside risk up to 2.54×, pooled conformal coverage swung 90.46%→67.80%, and sub-grade T1 sparsity blocked 77.82% of holdout Apple lots vs B2. Training dual-head estimators on uncensored payoff Y_full with validation-frozen penalty λ* = 0.15 plus grade-aware T1 raises holdout return to ₹479.17/qtl—beating B1 (+₹129.16), B2 (+₹32.51, p = 0.0016), and MG_v1 (+₹26.38), winning trap-free N = 10,162 open yards (₹533.75/qtl), and lifting 2026 HP Graded Apples +34.2% (₹812.08/qtl)."

6.2 The 5 Non-Negotiable Red-Lines (Never Overclaim These in Viva!)

  1. NEVER claim Theorem 1 exchangeability guarantees for Stage I or Stage II CRC: Stage-I coverage is empirical (78.85% val / 79.07% holdout) and Stage-II (n_l+1)/(n_d+1)≤0.095 (λ*=0.15 for Rung 3; 0.10 for Rung 2) is a Val_2025H1 (N=42,794) calibration heuristic adapted from Angelopoulos et al. (2024)—non-stationary crop prices and varying n_disp(λ) break Theorem 1 assumptions.
  2. NEVER pass Stage-II MandiGuard-CRC (₹479.17) off as pre-registered Stage I: Keep commit e421d15 Stage I (₹452.79) strictly separate from [POST-DIAGNOSTIC / VALIDATION-CALIBRATED] Stage II (anti-HARKing discipline).
  3. NEVER claim an autonomous LLM/RL agent or beating point-ML mean on open yards: Zero runtime LLM/RL calls; and on N=10,162 guaranteed-open yards, B3 still tops unconditional mean (₹553.22 vs MandiGuard-CRC ₹533.75) at 2.1× LTR (14.77% vs 7.14%) and 10× deeper CVaR10%.
  4. NEVER claim live farmer weighment receipts or full multi-year official API archival: Dual-Tier Exp 14 audits 172 XML keys + 2,042 149-day AGMARKNET 2.0 keys; truck hire, Q10 rot, and diversion penalties remain modeled; 22/22 pytest checks prove deterministic code, Dual-Tier parity, & zero future leakage—not field economics.
  5. NEVER present Appendix illustrations (Exp 11–13b) as primary thesis contributions.

6.3 Complete Master Viva Q&A Bank (All 50 Tough Examiner Questions)

Group A — Motivation, Novelty & Agricultural Economics (Q1–Q9)

Q1. In one sentence, what is "Phantom Spatial Arbitrage"?
An apparent cross-mandi profit spread on price boards that turns negative or fails to execute once highway freight, state charges, variety/grade mismatches, closed destination yards, ambient rot, and arrival price drops are included (40.46% loss rate across 63,040 naive dispatches).
Q2. Why didn't you just predict tomorrow's mandi price like most ML papers?
When yards are open on arrival day (N=10,162, Exp 15), point-ML B3 earns higher mean (₹553.22/qtl) at 2.2× LTR (14.77%) and 10× deeper tail (-₹362.40). Across the full market (N=69,526), B3 loses 45.28% of the time (65.65% traps, ₹330.85/qtl)—worse than naive B1—because it lacks T1 openness checks and T4 downside buffers.
Q3. Why is MandiGuard scientific decision support rather than "simple if-else business rules"?
Verbal rule router B6 loses -₹20.85/qtl vs MandiGuard (higher traps, 34.9% more calls); removing T4 conformal LCB raises LTR 9.97%→16.89% and crashes CVaR -₹37.89→-₹397.19; and ascending-cost gating beats upfront B4 by +₹104.54/qtl at B=6.
Q4. What happened to your earlier multi-ensemble EVA-Mandi attempt? Why pivot?
Stacking 9 ensembles, Duan smearing, and Knowledge-Gradient integrals over small HP Apple subsets failed 4/5 pre-registered hypotheses and trailed a staleness filter. Preserving that archive untouched, we pivoted cleanly to multi-state physical arbitrage with transparent engineering math, supporting H1, H3, H4.
Q5. Why is your local-sale option (REFUSE_PHANTOM_SPREAD) theoretically justified?
Chow (1970) and Franc et al. (2023) show abstaining is Bayes-optimal whenever false-positive mistake cost (sunk logistics + rot + diversion up to -₹1,062.66/qtl tail) far outweighs safe deterministic local realization (₹0).
Q6. How are truckload size and household income grounded?
Directly from NSO NSS Report No. 587 (77th Round): Potato/Onion harvests average 29.33–38.73 qtl (grounding 30-qtl mini-truck) and net monthly household crop income averages ₹3,798—making +₹102.78/qtl (+₹3,083.5/load) 81.2% of monthly crop income.
Q7. How do AgriMarket AI (2026) and Mandi Cast (2026) differ from MandiGuard?
They compute point gains using Haversine distances or weather price covariates without exact variety matching, arrival-weekday openness checks, Q10 transit spoilage, or selective conformal refusal—placing them in the B1/B3 baseline family.
Q8. Which crop suffers the highest phantom-loss rate, and why?
Onion (48.69% LTR under B1, ₹53.61 net on ₹704.50 spread) because slim margins are absorbed by ₹138.07 freight and ₹484.23 variety traps/drops. Apple suffers largest absolute erosion (₹3,499.8→₹1,982.36 traps/drops), and Tomato has highest market decay (3.25%/24h).
Q9. Why did naive B1 get a higher Tomato mean (₹547.64) than MandiGuard (₹522.48)?
B1 chases rare scarcity spikes that boost averages while losing money 32.38% of the time (1 in 3 trips). MandiGuard cuts Tomato episode losses to 5.09% and still beats B2 Fresh+OSRM (₹484.64) by +₹37.84/qtl.

Group B — Data Provenance, Official Anchors & Physical Model (Q10–Q19)

Q10. Where did your 10-year mandi data come from, and what did Dual-Tier Exp 14 verify?
Public AGMARKNET archive mirror (42.72M raw rows streamed with SHA-256 checksums). Dual-Tier Exp 14 verifies: Tier 1 (2023-10-18, 172 keys vs data.gov.in Resource 9ef84268-d588-465a-a308-a864a43d0070 XML: 100.0% Min/Max, 99.42% Modal parity) and Tier 2 (149-day direct official AGMARKNET 2.0 export, 2,042 matched market–variety–grade–day rows: 100.00% Min/Max/Modal parity).
Q11. How did you prevent survivorship bias when picking 178 core markets?
Markets were eligible and top-30 ranked per state using strictly calendar 2024 trading days (28 eligible in HP → 178 yards)—never peeking into 2025–2026 holdout closures.
Q12. Where did base spoilage rates come from? Were they tuned?
Zero tuning: taken verbatim from MoFPI/NABCONS (2022) Annexure-II Table-2 (PIB PRID 2151371): Tomato 3.25%, Onion 1.96%, Apple 1.64%, Potato 0.86%.
Q13. Don't you lack live farmer weighment receipts for freight, rot, and diversion penalties?
Yes—disclosed openly in Section 8. Trucking fees, Q10 rot, and diversion penalties are modeled rather than field-measured; yet observed AGMARKNET traps/drops drive ₹714.90/qtl erosion vs ₹68.76 spoilage, all 9/9 Exp 6 cells stay positive, and Exp 15 isolates fair observed cohorts and crossover sweeps.
Q14. Why do cross-district APMC fees differ across your 6 states?
Agricultural marketing is a State subject (PIB 154554): KA & GJ waive F&V fees (0.5% user fee); HP exempts veg (0.5%) except Apple (1.0%); MH charges 1.0% inside APMC; MP & UP levy 1.5%. Verified state rules lift spreads +₹7.12/qtl vs uniform 1.5% (Exp 6).
Q15. Why does Himachal Pradesh carry a 1.45× freight multiplier?
Grounded directly in GoHP Economic Survey 2025–26 Table 28: 91.59% (39,465 / 43,091 km) of HP motorable roads are single-lane mountain roads.
Q16. What happened when Open-Meteo hit daily rate limits on 43 northern grids?
We respected HTTP 429 cleanly. 145/145 realized ERA5 completed, plus 102/145 native NWP cells. The 43 remaining cells used a causal 2024 Ridge nowcaster using only day ≤ t ERA5 (1.047°C MAE, verified by pytest), and Exp 2b confirmed +₹31.82/qtl over B2 in the 4 full-NWP states.
Q17. How did you prevent geocoding errors (Neemuch/Gonda homonym mismatches)?
Enforced admin2 district-alias validation and a hard ≤110 km Haversine check against District HQ coordinates across all 220 mandis (checked in pytest).
Q18. How do you handle clerks entering "Onion", "Other", and "FAQ" interchangeably?
Canonicalize generic commodity name, "Other", and "FAQ" to "Standard" and unify spellings ("Deshi"→"Desi"), while preserving commercial cultivars ("Red", "Hybrid", "Royal Delicious").
Q19. What did the Live November 2026 AGMARKNET query check (Exp 8) show?
22 live queries on agmarknet.gov.in (Nov 17, 2026) found 11/22 (50.0%) benchmark corridors reported zero trades across the entire preceding 7 days.

Group C — ML, Conformal Bounds, Statistics & Limitations (Q20–Q35)

Q20. Explain Conformal Prediction (T4) in plain English.
Check how badly your forecast over-predicted across the last 400 settled trips, take the 80th-percentile worst downside miss (e.g., 8%), and subtract it from today's forecast so ~80% of arrivals clear your floor.
Q21. Doesn't Conformal Prediction assume i.i.d. exchangeability—violated by prices?
Yes—disclosed candidly. Because seasons break strict exchangeability, we verify empirical chronological coverage directly (78.85% val, 79.07% holdout) and test adaptive ACI in Appendix A.1.
Q22. Why train on 2024 only and never refit weights on 2025–2026?
Freezing tree weights in 2024 guarantees a clean 15-month out-of-time robustness test without holdout refitting leakage; only the 400-sample conformal residual window adapts causally.
Q23. How was safety_margin_inr = ₹50/qtl selected?
Swept over {50, 100, 150, 200, 250} strictly on Val_2025H1 (₹351.36/qtl mean, 9.68% LTR), locked in frozen_calibration.json and Git commit e421d15 before unblinding holdout.
Q24. Why did H2 (MandiGuard > B2 Mean) fail significance (p = 0.27)?
B2 ties MandiGuard on overall mean (₹446.66 vs ₹452.79; +₹6.13 is cluster noise). MandiGuard trades risky marginal dispatches (48.66% vs 62.11%) to halve loss rate (9.97% vs 18.11%) and reduce tail loss (-₹37.89 vs -₹436.67).
Q25. Why use Two-Way Mandi × 2-Week-Block Bootstrap instead of a paired t-test?
Episodes correlate within the same mandi over time and across mandis sharing weekly shocks. Resampling 174 mandis × 23 two-week blocks together prevents artificially narrow CIs (yielding [+₹48.66, +₹153.45] for H1) with Phipson–Smyth + Holm control.
Q26. In Exp 4, why does removing T3 slightly raise overall mean by ₹2.46/qtl?
T3 + T4 stack conservatively; dropping T3 admits 1.52% extra hot/rainy trips whose spot spikes beat modeled rot slightly overall, while keeping T3 protects the 21,656 extreme-weather episodes (LTR 11.39%→10.10%, CVaR -₹67.49→-₹57.11).
Q27. On HP Graded Apples (Exp 3), why did B2 earn ₹1,150.83 vs Stage-I MandiGuard ₹605.06—and what did Exp 16 prove really happened?
Initially we guessed wide T4 conformal bounds blocked scarce 2026 Grade A lots. Exp 16 disproved that: 77.82% of holdout refusals vs B2 (82.75% warmup) were blocked at T1 due to sub-grade rolling sparsity (open_prob_14d < 0.50), vs only 22.18% at T4. Stage I still cut traps 7× (94.14%→13.24%), and Stage-II grade-aware T1 lifts Apple mean +34.2% to ₹812.08/qtl.
Q28. Is MandiGuard an autonomous LLM agent? Why no GPT-4 at decision time?
No—deterministic risk-gated decision-support system. Avoiding runtime LLMs guarantees <0.1 ms latency, ₹0 token fee, zero hallucinations, and SMS/edge feasibility.
Q29. Why did 3-module coordinator B5 earn -₹15.40/qtl less than unified MandiGuard?
Passing coarse ₹150 profit buckets loses boundary precision near the ₹50/qtl threshold without saving calls (8.76 vs 8.75).
Q30. Does your model transfer to an unseen state (Exp 9)?
Yes: Leave-One-State-Out zero-shot transfer beat B1 in 6/6 held-out states (+₹11.50 to +₹424.19/qtl), cutting arrival drops to 3.34%–9.72% (vs 45.3%–55.7%).
Q31. What are the top rejection reasons across all 69,526 episodes (Exp 7)?
Dispatch 48.66% (12.30 calls); T1 Variety/Stale 25.48% (3.64 calls); T4 Arrival Reversion 17.58%; T1 Closed Risk 5.34% (3.04 calls); T2 Freight 2.24%; T3 Weather 0.71%.
Q32. Why model +1/+2 wait days (₹25/day detention) instead of immediate abandonment?
Mirrors real trucker behavior around rotating mid-week yard closures: drivers wait 1–2 mornings paying parking and extra decay before liquidating or diverting.
Q33. What happens under freight spikes or refrigerated trucks (Exp 6)?
Across 9/9 grid cells in [0.75×..1.25×] freight × [0.5×..1.5×] spoilage, MandiGuard beats B1 (+₹82.62 to +₹121.42/qtl), beats B2 at 1.0–1.5× rot (+₹5.27 to +₹14.50), and matches B2 within -₹1.52/qtl at 0.5× rot.
Q34. Why bound corridors to 15–500 km intra-state?
Reflects typical 30-qtl smallholder single-truck dispatch without inter-state permits; 1,500+ km interstate wholesale corridors remain future work.
Q35. How can someone reproduce all experiments independently?
Run notebooks/colab_standalone_reproduction.ipynb + colab_data_pack.tar.gz (4.83 MB) in Google Colab in under 3 minutes, or run pytest locally (reproducing Stage I, Stage II CRC, Dual-Tier Exp 14, and Appendix checks).

Group D — 10-Year Scale, Appendix Illustrations & Tough Probes (Q36–Q44)

Q36. Does MandiGuard hold up across GST, COVID, Export Curbs, and El-Niño (2017–2026)?
Across 661,192 matched episodes over 6 regimes (Exp 10), causally expanding MandiGuard holds LTR to 8.78%–12.03% (vs 39.18%–44.29% naive) and beats B1 by +₹165.14/qtl during 2024 El-Niño.
Q37. Does training on 8 years (3.44M rows) beat 1 year (2024, 702k rows)?
Only +₹2.15/qtl (₹454.94 vs ₹452.79/qtl, Exp 10b): shifting spread regimes make recent fit + conformal bounds far more valuable than stale volume.
Q38. (Appendix Exp 11) How did Quantile GBDT, Deep MLP, Bandits, and ACI perform?
Direct_Quantile_GBDT_Q20 reached ₹459.02/qtl on 6 states; Deep_MLP_Conformal reached ₹615.34 on HP Apple; MandiGuard_ACI trimmed HP Apple CVaR10% 27.6% (-₹102.76→-₹74.42).
Q39. (Appendix Exp 12) What is the real & modeled API cost picture?
Actual project API spend = ₹0.00 (public portals, OSRM, open climate grids, local CPU inference). Under illustrative ₹0.05/call commercial pricing (Exp 12), caching OSRM + local CPU T4 drops live calls to 5.53 (₹2,764/10k queries vs ₹7,868 B4), and ₹250 satisficing exit hits 3.84 calls (-75.6% cost, ₹1,922/10k). Crucially, API rupee savings are minor vs crop profits; reducing calls mainly boosts rural 2G/3G responsiveness and avoids government API throttling.
Q40. (Appendix Exp 13/13b) What do FPO pooling, Split-Lot, and Spoilage Clock illustrate?
90-qtl shared FPO trucks (0.70×) raise gain to ₹477.28/qtl; 50/50 Top-2 splitting cuts closed traps 39% (16.17%→9.85%); Tomato 15% Q10 safe window drops from 110.8h (20°C) to 24.1h (42°C) inside ≤160-char SMS cards.
Q41. Isn't H4 (44.4% fewer calls than B4) obvious by construction?
Yes—fewer average calls (8.75 vs 15.74) follow directly by ordering cheap T1 checks first. The empirical benefit shows under tight query budgets (B=6, Exp 5: +₹104.54/qtl over B4).
Q42. How thoroughly was the archive mirror checked against official government servers?
Dual-Tier Exp 14 verified 172 keys on 2023-10-18 vs official data.gov.in XML (100% Min/Max, 99.42% Modal) AND 2,042 matched rows across 149 trading days of direct AGMARKNET 2.0 exports (100.00% Min/Max/Modal) + 22 live Nov-2026 queries.
Q43. How do you defend Exp 15 if missing 3d entries have zero penalty or all yards are open?
Dual-view proof: View 1 crossover leads through 0.5×/5% (+₹42.43/qtl vs B1) and crosses only at 0.0×/0% (-₹10/qtl, holding LTR at 6.09% vs 18.52%); View 2 fair matched open-yard cohort (N=10,162) beats B1/B2 while proving B3 needs T1+T4 on full markets.
Q44. What do your 22/22 pytest tests actually prove?
Deterministic code reproducibility, SHA-256 data manifest parity, Dual-Tier Exp 14 & Stage-II Exp 16–17 consistency, district HQ coordinate bounds, bootstrap/Holm arithmetic, and zero future leakage—NOT real-world field economics without live truck receipts.

Group E — Stage-II [POST-DIAGNOSTIC / VALIDATION-CALIBRATED] Autopsy & MandiGuard-CRC (Q45–Q50)

Q45. What is Censored-Arrival Survivorship Bias (Exp 16A), and how much did it distort Stage I?
Stage-I dropna(target_ret) discarded 55.83% of raw 2024 corridors (12.64% post-T1). Exact d0 open rate falls from 89.10% (0d) to 62.63% (3d in train; 62.97% holdout), causing complete-case Q20 downside returns to understate true uncensored tail drops by 1.82–2.00× (Train) and up to 2.54× on Holdout (-10.55% vs -26.82%).
Q46. What is the Heteroscedastic Coverage Illusion (Exp 16B) in Stage-I bounds?
Pooled additive quantiles masked a 21.07–22.66 pp quartile coverage collapse: on Holdout, MG_v1 hit 90.46% coverage in calm Q1 markets (over-cushioning 6.04% vs 1.98% true error) while dropping to 67.80% in volatile Q4 markets (8.89% cushion vs 17.08% true Q80 error; Val 88.91%→67.84%).
Q47. How does MandiGuard-CRC score routes, and do you claim Angelopoulos et al. (2024) Theorem 1 guarantees?
Dual 2024 heads (regression μ̂ + raw HistGradientBoostingClassifier.predict_proba risk p̂_loss) trained on 274,296 settled profitable post-T1 uncensored routes Y_full score Score = μ̂ − λ*·P_loc·p̂_loss (requiring Score>₹50 & μ̂>₹50). Sweeping λ ∈ [0, 1.20] on clean Val_2025H1 (N=42,794, arr_dt≤2025-05-31) and stopping at the first feasible point (break) via (n_l+1)/(n_d+1)≤0.095 freezes λ* = 0.15 (Rung 2 strict T1 freezes at 0.10; zero holdout tuning). We explicitly do NOT claim Theorem 1 guarantees because agri prices violate exchangeability and n_disp(λ) varies with λ; we use it strictly as an empirical validation heuristic audited out-of-sample.
Q48. Why keep Stage I (₹452.79) frozen instead of replacing it with Stage II (₹479.17)?
Zero-HARKing discipline (Nosek et al. 2018): H1–H4 were pre-registered in commit e421d15 for Stage I. Any post-diagnostic fix discovered from Stage-I failures must be cleanly quarantined as [POST-DIAGNOSTIC / VALIDATION-CALIBRATED] alongside causal rungs (Rung 0→3) proving +₹26.38/qtl vs MG_v1 (p=0.0002) and +₹32.51/qtl vs B2 (p=0.0016).
Q49. Could MandiGuard-CRC just overfit to simulated closed-yard penalties in Y_full?
Tested directly on trap-free Matched_AllTopK_Observed_d0 (N=10,162, zero simulated penalties): MandiGuard-CRC reaches ₹533.75/qtl at 7.14% LTR and -₹35.00 CVaR, beating MG_v1 (+₹22.86), B1 (+₹61.24), and B2 (+₹63.76) while cutting B3's 14.77% LTR in half.
Q50. Why did MandiGuard-CRC jump +34.2% on HP Apples (₹605.06→₹812.08) yet still trail B2 (₹1,150.83)?
Grade-aware T1 removed 77.82% false sparsity blocks, lifting Grade A from ₹205.46 to ₹477.56/qtl (LTR 20.0%→11.54%) and Grade B to ₹852.01/qtl. Remaining gap vs B2 reflects safety–volume tradeoff: B2 accepts 28.43% LTR and -₹272.50 CVaR (-₹4,472.90 on Grade B), vs CRC's -₹113.40 CVaR.
